title: feature_request(img): src attribute for lazy loading
body: (*I was sent here [**from the repository validator/validator**](https://github.com/validator/validator/issues/750).*) ### 1. Summary For JavaScript lazy loading scripts `src` images attribute not required; no recommended use it. It would be nice, if the absence of `src` will not error, if lazy loading accepted. ### 2. Practice + [**Stack Overflow answer**](https://stackoverflow.com/a/41533483/5951529): > A common approach to lazy-loading images is to set the `src` to a very small image, sometimes a 1x1px gif, and once the user scrolls and the image is on the screen replace the `src` with the real one. ### 3. Example + [**sources**](https://repl.it/@Kristinita/KiraJQueryLazyFancyBox-Demo) + [**HTML**](https://kirajquerylazyfancybox-demo--kristinita.repl.co/) Nu Html Checker [**show errors**](https://validator.w3.org/nu/?doc=https%3A%2F%2Fkirajquerylazyfancybox-demo--kristinita.repl.co%2F): > Element `img` is missing required attribute `src`. I use: ```html ``` Instead of: ```html ``` [**And it works**](https://stackoverflow.com/a/54445455/5951529). ### 4. Argumentation #### 4.1. Performance + Lazyload official documentation — “[**Do NOT use placeholder images**](https://github.com/verlok/lazyload#do-not-use-placeholder-images)”: > We do not recommend using a placeholder image (like a transparent pixel GIF) in your HTML. > > * For **best perceived performance, leave the `src` and `srcset` attributes blank**. Doing so, the image will be shown as soon as LazyLoad starts loading the image. See [**this video**](https://youtu.be/2E3ociaFJS0) or [**this pen**](https://codepen.io/verlok/pen/bKYggE?editors=0110) to test the difference (remember to disable the cache and to set a slower connection speed if you have a very fast one). > * If you put anything in the `src` (like a transparent GIF), then LazyLoad starts loading the image but it won't be shown by browsers until the new image is loaded, leading to a **worse perceived performance**. > > It's safe not to put any value in the `src` nor `srcset` attributes, even if your HTML won't validate by a static code analyzer. The reason is that once JavaScript is executed, those values will be set by LazyLoad. For SEO, if the client is a crawler like Googlebot, it will be detected by LazyLoad which will fix the HTML. #### 4.2. Extra attribute [**JQuery Lazy owner say**](https://github.com/eisbehr-/jquery.lazy/issues/102#issuecomment-321979124): > Of course you get this error, because *src* is a mandatory attribute for *img* tag. But no browser will have a problem when you miss the `src` attribute. It's just a warning you can ignore. > > But solving this issue is pretty easy. Just add an empty *src* attribute to all your *img* tags. That is generally a good practice to do so. Users add extra `src="link/to/placeholder"` only for validator; it not really needed. #### 4.3. Tools For example, extra `src` attribute add problems for: + [**Slick**](https://github.com/kenwheeler/slick/issues/1062#issuecomment-75427924) (~23000 GitHub stars) + [**Swiper**](https://github.com/nolimits4web/Swiper/issues/1476#issue-113090758) (~19000 GitHub stars) ### 5. Not helped Yes, I read about [**`lazyload` attribute**](https://css-tricks.com/a-native-lazy-load-for-the-web-platform/) and **#699**. But: 1. We wait implementations 1. We need waiting, when browsers will support this. Thanks.
